# Intents

**Symbols:** 25.1% of Apple's iOS API (731 of 2909, exact) · **Rows:** 50% (4: 2 ✅ 2 ❌) · **iOS:** 10.0+
<!-- /generated:header -->

**Area:** [App extensions & system integration](../COVERAGE.md#system) · **Apple:** [Intents](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/intents) · **Issues:** [`area:system`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Asystem)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** isim's own Objective-C framework (`isim/frameworks/Intents`, `INSiriRunner.m`), with a Siri card.

## API

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SiriKit (Intents) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the Intents framework (messages: `INSendMessageIntent`, `INSearchForMessagesIntent`; calls: `INStartCallIntent`; media: `INPlayMediaIntent`; lists and notes: `INAddTasksIntent`, `INCreateNoteIntent`) with their resolution results (success / needsValue / disambiguation / confirmationRequired / unsupported(forReason:) / notRequired), response codes and the handling protocols (completion and async forms). The simulated Siri understands fixed English phrasings and the structured `siri intent CLASS key=value` form (docs/SCRIPTING.md; no speech recognition) and runs the conversation in the app's Intents extension (`com.apple.intents-service`, `INExtension` `handler(for:)`, `IntentsSupported`) or in the app (`INIntentsSupported`, `application(_:handlerFor:)`; `.handleInApp` via `application(_:handle:completionHandler:)`): resolve, confirm (messages are read back), handle; `.continueInApp` / app-launch failures open the app with an `NSUserActivity` carrying its `INInteraction`. Intents UI extensions (`INUIHostedViewControlling`) draw Siri's card. `INPreferences.requestSiriAuthorization` (system alert, remembered; Settings > the app > Siri; the `com.apple.developer.siri` entitlement is required), `INInteraction.donate` / delete (Siri Suggestions in Shortcuts; Siri donates what it handled), `INVoiceShortcutCenter`, `INUIAddVoiceShortcutViewController` (phrase typed) / edit / `INUIAddVoiceShortcutButton`, voice shortcuts run by their phrase. Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit, per iOS version). Not in isim: other domains (payments, rides, workouts, car, restaurant, ...), Contacts-based person resolution by Siri, `INInteraction.dateInterval` (no `NSDateInterval` in isim's Foundation) |
| Custom intents (`.intentdefinition`; `INObject`, `INEnumResolutionResult`, `INObjectResolutionResult`, `INIntegerResolutionResult`, `INDoubleResolutionResult`, `INURLResolutionResult`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: `isim build` generates Xcode's Swift classes from each `.intentdefinition` (enums as `@objc enum: Int` with their resolution results, custom types as `INObject` subclasses with theirs, per intent the `INIntent` subclass with `@NSManaged` parameters, its `…Handling` protocol with Xcode's selectors, the response code enum (custom codes from 100) and the `INIntentResponse` subclass with `code` and a factory per custom code) and copies the definition into the bundle; `INIntent`, `INIntentResponse` and `INObject` subclasses keep `@NSManaged` / `@dynamic` properties with their values (objects and scalars). Siri runs custom intents in the app or its Intents extension like the system ones: values from `siri intent CLASS key=value` converted to the parameters' types, missing values asked for with the definition's primary prompt, `resolve<Param>For<Intent>`, `confirm`, `handle`, and the response code's format string spoken with its parameters. `INTENTS_CODEGEN_LANGUAGE = None` turns generation off; Objective-C classes are not generated (the Swift classes are `@objc`). Tested (HelloCustomIntents: test_generated_intent_classes, test_custom_intent_in_app, test_custom_intent_with_siri) |
| Types not yet in isim (iOS 17 and earlier) | ❌ | ≤17 | not implemented, found by the 2026-10 sweep: `INAccountTypeResolutionResult`, `INActivateCarSignalIntent`, `INActivateCarSignalIntentHandling`,
